history.dynasty: Legend: King Vikramaditya; Maratha (Ahilyabai Holkar, 18th c. renovation)
history.period: Ancient (8th c. per some sources - uncertain); present structure 18th c. Maratha
history.summary: A Shakti Peetha of Ujjain: the Shiva Purana places it among the 51 Shakti Peethas, where Goddess Sati's elbow is believed to have fallen. Legend credits King Vikramaditya with building the temple; one account says Adi Shankaracharya established the shrine in the 8th century (uncertain). The present dark-crimson Maratha structure, with four entrances and two towering deepmalas carrying 726 lamp holders lit during Navratri, was renovated and expanded in the 18th century, particularly under Ahilyabai Holkar. The sanctum enshrines Harsiddhi flanked by Maha Saraswati and Kali, and the temple stands ~350 m from the Mahakaleshwar Temple. No CSV town/state errors.

name: Harsiddhi Temple
town_description: Ancient city on the Shipra (Kshipra) River in Madhya Pradesh, one of Hinduism's seven Sapta Puri, home to the Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga and the Simhastha Kumbh Mela held every 12 years.

travel.airport: Devi Ahilya Bai Holkar Airport, Indore (~55 km)
travel.railway: Ujjain Junction, connected to all major stations of India
travel.road: Well connected by road; regular buses from Indore, Bhopal and other MP cities

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; Navratri for the deepmala lighting
visitor_information.opening_hours: Not confirmed by sources; evening aarti around 6:45-7:30 PM reported (verify)
